notes: Original title/authors verified against the supplied canonical source. Rendered PDF pp. 10–11 inspected for column layout and OCR. Target is Study 4, preference for consistent versus inconsistent information by quantity, but selection-focus condition and exact contrast are unspecified. Candidate quantity-by-selection chi-square interactions, printed p. 241: no induction N=52, chi-square(1)=13.18, p=.001; quality focus N=51, chi-square(1)=0.32, p=.57; direction focus N=52, chi-square(1)=7.42, p=.01. Additional within-condition preference candidates on p. 241: no induction/2 pieces N=26, chi-square(1)=3.85, p=.05; no induction/10 pieces N=26, chi-square(1)=9.85, p=.003; quality/2 pieces N=24, chi-square(1)=4.17, p=.04; quality/10 pieces N=27, chi-square(1)=8.33, p=.01; direction/2 pieces N=25, chi-square(1)=17.64, p=.001; direction/10 pieces N=27, chi-square(1)=0.93, p=.33. Omnibus three-way interaction across quantity, selection criterion, and selection, pp. 240–241: printed Z=-2.02, CI (-3.54, -0.05), SE=0.89, p=.04. Footnote 5 gives another three-way term Z=-1.55, CI (-3.47, 0.41), SE=0.99, p=.12. These are separate tests. Method reports 155 student participants, randomly assigned to six between-subject conditions; this whole-study participation count is not assigned as the analytic N for an unspecified target. Candidate Ns above are explicit participant Ns printed with their individual chi-square tests; exclusions are not stated in the inspected Study 4 Method/Results. No N is derived from degrees of freedom and no sample counts are summed. No metric conversion. Original-side fields remain null because correspondence is unresolved. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders, not source-unavailability conclusions.
